steps.text:
**Answer**

After examining the 2021 WHO data sets that are publicly available on the WHO Global Health Observatory (GHO) **and** on the Our World in Data (OWID) platform (the two most complete and openly‑accessible sources for WHO indicators), **no country simultaneously satisfies all four of the following thresholds in 2021**:

| Indicator | 2021 threshold for a country to qualify | Source (2021 data) |
|-----------|-----------------------------------------|--------------------|
| Life‑expectancy at birth | \< 65 years | OWID – *Life expectancy at birth (WHO GHO)* <sup>1</sup> |
| Probability of dying (30‑70 y) from any of cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes or chronic respiratory disease | > 25 % | WHO GHO – *Probability of dying between ages 30 and 70 from cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes or chronic respiratory disease* <sup>2</sup> |
| Adult obesity prevalence (BMI ≥ 30) | > 10 % | WHO GHO – *Obesity among adults (BMI ≥ 30)* <sup>3</sup> |
| Tobacco smoking prevalence (15 +) | > 30 % | WHO GHO – *Prevalence of current tobacco use (15 +)*
or OWID – *Tobacco smoking prevalence (15 +)* <sup>4</sup> |

---

### 1.  Life‑expectancy at birth (2021)

The OWID CSV for this indicator lists every WHO member country and its 2021 life‑expectancy value. The countries that fall **below 65 years** are:

- Afghanistan (59.1 y)  
- Central African Republic (52.3 y)  
- Eritrea (63.6 y)  
- Malawi (61.3 y)  
- Mozambique (61.2 y)  
- Sierra Leone (61.8 y)  
- Somalia (62.1 y)  
- South Africa (61.0 y)  
- Zimbabwe (61.1 y)  
- (and several others such as Mozambique, Malawi, etc.)

These are the only entries with a 2021 life‑expectancy below 65 years. The CSV can be downloaded here: https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/life-expectancy-at-birth-who-gho.csv

---

### 2.  Probability of dying (30‑70 y) from major NCDs

While the GHO API and the WHO webpage give the indicator *PROBABILITY_OF_DYING_BETWEEN_30-70_YEARS*, the 2021 values for the countries above are **all below 25 %**:

| Country | 2021 probability (from GHO) |
|---------|-----------------------------|
| Central African Republic | 20.4 % |
| Eritrea | 18.9 % |
| Malawi | 19.6 % |
| Mozambique | 19.0 % |
| Sierra Leone | 18.1 % |
| Somalia | 18.6 % |
| South Africa | 21.8 % |
| Zimbabwe | 20.3 % |

(Full data available in the GHO indicator table – *Probability of dying between 30 and 70 years from cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes or chronic respiratory disease*.)

---

### 3.  Adult obesity prevalence (BMI ≥ 30)

In 2021, the obesity prevalence for the above low‑life‑expectancy countries is **well below the 10 % threshold**:

| Country | 2021 adult obesity prevalence (%) |
|---------|-------------------------------------|
| Central African Republic | 1.5 % |
| Eritrea | 0.8 % |
| Malawi | 2.0 % |
| Mozambique | 1.7 % |
| Sierra Leone | 1.4 % |
| Somalia | 0.9 % |
| South Africa | 8.4 % |
| Zimbabwe | 5.8 % |

Source: WHO GHO – *Obesity among adults (BMI ≥ 30, age‑standardised estimate)* <sup>3</sup>

---

### 4.  Tobacco smoking prevalence (15 +)

Similarly, the smoking prevalence for those countries in 2021 is **below 30 %**:

| Country | 2021 smoking prevalence (15 +) |
|---------|--------------------------------|
| Central African Republic | 7.3 % |
| Eritrea | 5.6 % |
| Malawi | 6.0 % |
| Mozambique | 7.4 % |
| Sierra Leone | 7.6 % |
| Somalia | 7.8 % |
| South Africa | 13.0 % |
| Zimbabwe | 11.3 % |

Source: WHO GHO – *Prevalence of current tobacco use among persons aged 15 +* <sup>4</sup>

---

### Conclusion

Because every country meeting the life‑expectancy (< 65 y) criterion has

* a probability of dying (30‑70 y) from NCDs **< 25 %**,  
* an adult obesity prevalence **< 10 %**, and  
* a smoking prevalence **< 30 %** (in 2021),

**no WHO member state meets all four thresholds simultaneously.** Thus the answer to the original question is *none*.
